stimuli.title: Isha, Riya, Deepa, Hema, Uma, Lata, Pia, Tara attend interviews, one per slot, on 7 and 21 March, April, May and June. Slots run in chronological order.
stimuli.body:

• Tara occupies June 21.
• Riya attends in May.
• Exactly 2 interview slots fall between the interviews of Isha and Pia.
• Riya attends on day 7 of a month.
• Riya attends after Hema.
• Exactly 1 interview slot falls between the interviews of Uma and Pia.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
savings digital growth = re vo ze
savings credit access = vo pa mi
digital credit banking = pa ni re
growth access banking = ni ze mi
savings digital banking = re vo ni
What is the code for “banking”?
questions.explanation: Answer: ni. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: savings = vo, digital = re, growth = ze, credit = pa, access = mi, banking = ni.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 50 km south, turns right and walks 84 km, then turns right and walks 15 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 91. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 35 km along the initial direction and 84 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(35² + 84²) = 91 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 27 km north, turns right and walks 24 km, then turns right and walks 9 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 30. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 18 km along the initial direction and 24 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(18² + 24²) = 30 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 75 km north, turns left and walks 168 km, then turns left and walks 5 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 182. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 70 km along the initial direction and 168 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(70² + 168²) = 182 km.

questions.stem: F is the mother of C. G is the son of C. B is the father of C. How is G related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. B is a parent of C, and G is C’s son. Hence G is B’s grandchild.

questions.stem: B is the brother of E. E is the mother of A. F is the father of B and E. How is B related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. B is the brother of A’s mother E. Therefore B is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: D is the only daughter of G. G is the father of D. A is the son of D. B is the sister of G. How is G related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. G is the father of D, and D is A’s mother. Thus G is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 48 candidates, a candidate is 11th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 35. New front rank = 11+3 = 14. Back rank = 48 − 14 + 1 = 35.

questions.stem: In a queue of 39 candidates, a candidate is 8th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 28. New front rank = 8+4 = 12. Back rank = 39 − 12 + 1 = 28.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹1950. It is marked above cost and sold at a 25% discount on marked price, earning 25% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 3250. Selling price = 1950 × 125/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.75 = 3250.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 26 days and B in 39 days. They work together for 2 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 22.67. Use 78 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 78 − 2×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: What is the difference (₹) between compound interest and simple interest on ₹32000 at 15% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
questions.explanation: Answer: 720. For 2 years, CI − SI = P(r/100)² = 32000 × (15/100)².

questions.stem: A vessel contains 50 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 10. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 10.

questions.stem: The average of 17 numbers is 48. One number, 60, is replaced and the average rises by 3. What is the new number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 111. Total increases by 17 × 3. New number = 60 + 51.

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 8 years, their combined age will be 80 years. Find the father’s present age.
questions.explanation: Answer: 48. Let daughter’s age be x. Father is 3x. 4x + 16 = 80; x = 16, so father = 48.
